questions.stem: Which of the following is a type of storm that originates over the ocean?
questions.solution: A cyclone is a type of storm that forms over warm ocean waters, typically in tropical regions. Thunderstorms, hailstorms, and tornadoes can occur over land or water but are not specifically defined as ocean-originating storms. Cyclones are characterized by their large scale and rotation, which develop due to the heat and moisture from the ocean.

questions.stem: What is the first aid for a person suffering from sunstroke?
choices: Wipe the body with cold water
Give the person water to drink
Make the person run in the sun
Cover the person with a blanket
questions.solution: Wiping the body with cold water helps lower the person's body temperature, which is critical in sunstroke. Giving water to a semi-conscious person can be dangerous, and running in the sun or covering with a blanket would increase body heat, worsening the condition.

questions.stem: What should you do if a person’s clothes catch fire on the street?
choices: Make the person roll on the ground
Help the person run to a safe place
Use a fan to cool the person down
Pour water directly on the person
questions.solution: Making the person roll on the ground suffocates the fire by cutting off its oxygen supply, which is the most effective way to put out flames on clothing. Running can fan the flames and make the situation worse. Using a fan may spread the fire, and pouring water could cause burns or be ineffective if the water source is not readily available.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a reason why people should avoid crowding at the site of an accident?
questions.solution: Crowding at an accident site may block emergency vehicles, preventing them from reaching those in need quickly. This is a direct and critical reason to avoid such behavior. choices: To make space for emergency vehicles
questions.solution: The main reason for avoiding crowding at the site of a major accident is to prevent further accidents. questions.stem: What can happen if a river's course changes after an earthquake?
choices: It will always lead to a drought
It can cause floods in some areas and droughts in others
It can cause landslides in nearby hills
It will always lead to a flood
questions.solution: When a river's course changes due to an earthquake, it can disrupt the natural flow of water, leading to areas receiving too much water (floods) and others receiving too little (droughts). Landslides may occur due to the shaking, but they are not a direct result of the river's new course. Droughts and floods are not guaranteed in all cases, so the idea that it will 'always' lead to either is incorrect.
